text:
Maya Singh: Heads-up — noticed a perf/quality regression after the fp8 kernel switch on canary. Several evals show slower p50 and some JSON fields get truncated for a subset of prompts.
Sam Ortiz: ugh. Is this the matmul change we rolled yesterday?
Maya Singh: looks correlated. Canary used matmul_fp8_opt, fallback to matmul_generic kicks in for long seqs. When fallback happens, KV cache alignment seems off and streaming chunks cut a final JSON field.
Eli Chen: any profiling data? perf-bot, can you paste the trace?
perf-bot: perf trace: https://perf.internal/redwood/trace/abcd1234 (summary below)
perf-bot: p50 tokens/s dropped from 680 -> 410 on fp8 route for seq_len distribution skewed to 1500-2200. kernel_switch_count=37, fallback_rate=0.42
Sam Ortiz: thanks. That fallback rate is huge. My hunch: quant calibration LUT now produces a narrower scale range for some layers, kernel chooser decides fp8 unsafe and falls back. The fallback path uses a different kv packing layout.
Maya Singh: repro script: ```python
# repro snippet
client = RedwoodClient(model='redwood-v1-mix', quant='fp8')
resp = client.generate(prompt, max_tokens=512, stream=True, seq_len=1800)
# observe truncated last field in streaming JSON
```
Grace Park: I ran a small local run — saw identical truncation on 3/5 seeds. Also eval delta: Rouge-L down ~1.9 on our structured-output eval set, halluc rate +3.1%.
Eli Chen: could be a KV pointer/offset mismatch when switching kernels mid-request. If kv cache buffer is differently aligned (pad handled differently), the streaming serializer may cut before finishing last token.
Sam Ortiz: suggested triage steps: 1) force fp8_opt for entire request (no fallback) to see if it stabilizes. 2) run with explicit old calibration tables (pre-3.14) to isolate LUT change. 3) add assert in runtime to validate kv offsets when kernel changes.
Maya Singh: did quick experiment: forcing fp8_opt end-to-end removes truncation but p50 still worse than baseline (so perf regression isn't only fallback).
Grace Park: I can roll back calibration on a canary for 50k requests tomorrow and compare evals. Assigning to me.
Eli Chen: I'll add a lightweight check to the KV cache write path to log offsets when kernel_switch_count > 0. Keep logs gated behind debug flag to avoid perf hit.
Sam Ortiz: I'll re-run microbench with different pad strategies (pad-left vs pad-right) to see if alignment sensitivity shows up. Also try forcing int8 kernel as a control.
Maya Singh: action items: Grace rollback cal+compare evals, Eli add KV offset asserts/logging, Sam benchmark pad/forced-int8, I'll prepare a minimal failing prompt set and create an eval job. We'll reconvene in #eng-runtime tomorrow EOD.
Grace Park: filing a ticket: INF-3842 (canary fp8 calib rollback + eval), linking perf trace.
Maya Singh: cool. also ping @platform-ops if we need a quick canary rollback window. :thumbsup:
Eli Chen: noting risk: if rollback fixes quality but not perf we still need kernel perf regression chase. Could be a kernel codegen change.
Sam Ortiz: FYI I saw a kernel compile tweak landed in 3.14 that changed GEMM tile size heuristics for A100. I'll diff that.
perf-bot: scheduled bake: canary-3.14 -> 3.13 compare job queued (job id job-7721).
Maya Singh: thanks everyone. saving failing prompts to /mnt/shared/triage/1718654321/failing_prompts.jsonl
Grace Park: grabbing them now and kicking off rollback run.
